question: What minimum miles-per-gallon rating must a vehicle achieve to qualify as an inherently low-emission vehicle under the MUTCD?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not specify any miles-per-gallon (fuel economy) rating for a vehicle to qualify as an inherently low-emission vehicle (ILEV). ILEV status is based on emissions certification by the EPA, not fuel economy: ILEVs are vehicles having no fuel vapor (hydrocarbon) emissions that are certified by the EPA under 40 CFR §88.311-93 and 40 CFR §88.312-93(c). There is no MPG threshold anywhere in the provided evidence. Standards (mandatory): - The Manual mandates only the meaning of the acronym itself: "The following acronyms and abbreviations, when used in this Manual, shall have the following meanings: ... 28. ILEV—inherently low emission vehicle." Guidance (recommended): - "The Inherently Low Emission Vehicle (ILEV) (R3-10a) sign (see Figure 2G-1) should be used when it is permissible for a properly labeled and certified ILEV, regardless of the number of occupants, to use an HOV lane." Note that eligibility hinges on being "properly labeled and certified," not on fuel economy. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 1D-1 lists "Inherently Low Emission Vehicle — ILEV" as an acceptable abbreviation without any performance criteria; [Image 5] shows the R3-10a "INHERENTLY LOW EMISSION VEHICLES ALLOWED" sign in Figure 2G-1 with no MPG-based qualification; [Image 8] contains Section 2G.04 text confirming ILEVs are defined by EPA emissions certification, not fuel economy. Citations: - Section 1C.03 Standard §1 (p.31) - Section 2G.04 Guidance §2 (p.412) - Section 2G.04 Support §3 (p.412) - Table 1D-1 (p.35)
gold_answer: The MUTCD does not specify this information. A correct response should state that the requested value or requirement cannot be determined from the manual rather than inventing an answer.
